observations: At least four head-like forms fill the frame: a dark-jawed shape at left in yellow and black, a gray-white skeletal form at center, a pink-outlined figure with blue horizontal bars at right, and a green-black shape with X-marked features at lower right.

Rows of teeth or jaw-like black-and-white marks repeat across at least four locations—left figure's open mouth, center figure's red-lined grin, the pink figure's blue bars, and a white-outlined jaw at bottom center.
A thin cream border frames the composition, and an nnxyz mark appears in the lower-left corner in red and yellow strokes; scattered symbols include circled letters and small hash marks.
reading: Overlapping head-forms crowd every inch of the surface, each staked out by a different color zone—yellow-black at left, gray-white at center, pink and blue at right, neon green at lower right. They share a jagged tooth motif that stitches them together even as their outlines compete. The small green face with its blunt X-eyes reads as almost comic against the tangled anatomy surrounding it, lending the scene a feeling of clashing tones—some loud, some buried under layers of overdrawn line.
contextAngle: Within the owned rawblocks subset, this work sits near the end of the title sequence. Its title neighbors, rawblocks #59 and #61, each center on a single dominant head, making this multi-figure density unusual for this stretch of the family.

connections.reason: Rawblocks #59 isolates one large head on a bright blue field, highlighting how #60 fragments similar skull vocabulary across four or more competing forms.
Nnotb #185 shares heavy yellow framing lines and an exposed-teeth grid but fills a single face to the edges, whereas #60 shrinks similar elements into a packed ensemble.

lookingQuestion: Where exactly do the color zones—yellow at left, gray-white at center, pink at right—stop belonging to one figure and start belonging to another?
ambiguities: The exact count of distinct figures is uncertain; overlapping lines make it unclear whether some shapes are separate heads or extensions of others.
Small text-like marks and circled symbols appear throughout but are not fully legible.
